PAGE TITLE: MANAGEMENT’S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS | FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE Sources of Funding

CHARTS:
- Title: Sources of Funding Comparison for FY 2024 and FY 2023 (IN MILLIONS)
  - Chart Type: Stacked column chart
  - Units: Millions
  - Legend: Spending Authority from Offsetting Collections, Prior Year Congressional Appropriations, Congressional Appropriations
  - Labeled Values:
    - 2024 (Total $30,051 Total): Spending Authority from Offsetting Collections: $1,840; Prior Year Congressional Appropriations: $3,335; Congressional Appropriations: $24,876
    - 2023 (Total $30,923 Total): Spending Authority from Offsetting Collections: $2,108; Prior Year Congressional Appropriations: $3,242; Congressional Appropriations: $25,573
- Title: Sources of Funding FY 2024 (IN MILLIONS)
  - Chart Type: Donut chart
  - Units: Millions
  - Center text: TOTAL FUNDING $30,051
  - Labeled Values:
    - Spending Authority from Offsetting Collections: 6% ($1,840)
    - Prior Year Congressional Appropriations: 11% ($3,335)
    - Congressional Appropriations: 83% ($24,876)

DIAGRAMS:
- Green background callout box:
  - Text: "Appropriations from Congress for the current fiscal year and unobligated balances from prior fiscal years."
  - Text: "Revenue from agreements with other governmental organizations or private entities."

KEY FACTS:
- In FY 2024, the total funds available for use by the Agency was $30 billion — a decrease of $872 million or three percent, compared to FY 2023.
- The $24.9 billion in appropriations from Congress for FY 2024 accounted for 83 percent of the total funds available for use by the Agency.
- Appropriations that remained available from prior years totaled $3.3 billion, 11 percent of NASA’s available resources in FY 2024.
- NASA’s FY 2024 funding also included $1.8 billion spending authority from offsetting collections, representing six percent of NASA’s available resources in FY 2024.
- In FY 2024, NASA obligated $27 billion of the $30 billion available for Agency programmatic and institutional objectives.
- The remaining $3 billion may be obligated until the funds' periods of availability expire.
